Oct 30, 23:29 UTC Resolved - On October 30, 2026, between 20:15 and 21:56 UTC, an advisory-publication-driven fan-out caused an unexpected saturation of network connections to the Dependabot alerts datastore. During this period we observed a high rate of write failures on this datastore; users saw elevated failure rates when dismissing or resolving Dependabot alerts, as well as failures when linking Dependabot update pull requests to Dependabot security alerts. We also observed delays in creating and updating security alerts that extended through November 2, 2026. The unexpected fan-out was caused by a missing job queue throttle after the queues for the fan-out work were migrated as part of system maintenance. We have restored the fan-out throttle and further isolated and throttled these processes to guard against further disruptions. Oct 30, 22:32 UTC Monitoring - The degradation has been mitigated. We are monitoring to ensure stability. Oct 30, 22:32 UTC Update - We have mitigated impact and are seeing recovery. We are monitoring for full recovery. Nov 3, 22:41 UTC Resolved - On November 3, 2026, between 15:00 UTC and 22:37 UTC, Git operations over HTTPS on GitHub.com were degraded. Clones, fetches, and pushes over HTTPS were slow, and some failed. For about half of Git HTTPS traffic, median response time rose from under 100 milliseconds to as high as 5 seconds. On average, the error rate was 0.65% and peaked at 1.29% of requests to the service. Git operations over SSH were not affected. This was due to a buildup of excess connections on the hosts that serve Git HTTPS traffic, which saturated their network capacity and caused slow and failed responses for all clients served by those hosts. We mitigated the incident by blocking a client traffic pattern at our load balancers and reloading them, which released the excess connections. The block also prevented some users of one third-party integration from performing Git operations over HTTPS until we removed it on November 4 at 13:26 UTC. We are working to alert on sustained Git HTTPS latency sooner and make load balancer mitigations take effect on existing connections immediately. Some Actions queues took additional time to drain after mitigation, and the incident was resolved at 19:23 UTC. The impact was triggered by maintenance on a cloud network gateway connecting an Actions service in the GitHub data center to Redis clusters in the Central US Azure region. The service's Redis client retried aggressively and redialed those connections. That produced a connection storm that saturated the gateway, with about 90% of connection attempts failing. Other services sharing the same network path were degraded as well. We mitigated the incident by removing the affected resources from rotation, which ended the connection storm and allowed the gateway to recover. We have already reduced the number of connection retries in the impacted service and are further improving retry behavior with jittered backoff, shorter connect timeouts, and retry budgets. These failures were caused by a scheduled maintenance event where GitHub migrated 7 tables between two MySQL clusters in our IAD and Azure Central US datacenters. One of the affected tables stores installation records for GitHub App server-to-server tokens (excluding Actions). However, in this case, the migration coincided with a scheduled cleanup job on the installation records table, which deleted approximately 59 million records from 0444-0617 UTC. As a result, the gh-ost tooling used in the migration experienced inter-cluster replication delays (up to 1 hour at peak). Oct 23, 08:05 UTC Resolved - On October 23, 2026, between 07:06 UTC and 07:27 UTC, GitHub Actions workflow run results were delayed. Job status, check run updates, and logs in the GitHub UI and API updated with an average delay of about 2 minutes, and some updates were delayed by up to about 7 minutes. During this window, a storage dependency that Actions uses to process workflow logs and artifacts throttled our requests. This slowed result processing, causing updates to queue up. The queue was fully processed by 07:27 UTC, shortly after the throttling stopped. To reduce the risk of recurrence, we have added several storage accounts to increase capacity, and we are working on additional steps to continue to scale. We are also working with our storage provider to understand why the throttling occurred, and improving how result processing handles storage throttling and how quickly we detect it.
